samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (बालग्रह is a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa: बालानां ग्रहः)
samasa.literal: overpowered by the seizers of children
samasa.sense: children afflicted by the spirits believed to seize the young

samasa.literal: in the breaking of a union
samasa.sense: when people bound together fall apart

morph.note: कारक is √कृ + ण्वुल् (-अक), an agent noun ‘maker’; neuter here to agree with the understood subject माहात्म्यम्.
Genitive plural of the r-stem नृ, with the long ṝ optional in this form; the Gita Press has नृणाम्, with ṇ after ṛ.

mantras.anvaya: (एतत् माहात्म्यं) बालग्रहाभिभूतानां बालानां शान्तिकारकम्, नृणां संघातभेदे च उत्तमं मैत्रीकरणम् (भवति)।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two nominal predicates of an unexpressed subject, the Māhātmya (named in 12.16): ‘(it is) a bringer of peace … and the best means of friendship …’.
mantras.lit: (It is) the bringer of relief for children overpowered by child-seizers, and, when a union among men is broken, the best means of making friendship.
mantras.tr: It brings peace to children seized by evil spirits, and when men who were bound together fall apart, it is the best way to make them friends again.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Evil spirits’ renders बालग्रह, a class of beings believed to afflict children; the subject ‘it’ (the Māhātmya) is supplied.

comm.t: Two further uses of the text: for children afflicted by bālagrahas, and for reconciling men whose union has broken. The subject, the Māhātmya, is carried over from the previous verses.

बालग्रह, ‘seizers of children’, are a class of beings named in the medical and Purāṇic literature as the cause of children’s illnesses; rites of protection against them were part of household religion, and the Devī here offers her Māhātmya as such a rite.

samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (बलहानि is a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa: बलस्य हानिः)
samasa.literal: that which makes the loss of strength
samasa.sense: that which robs (the wicked) of their power

samasa.vigraha: रक्षांसि च भूतानि च पिशाचाश्च, तेषाम्
samasa.sense: of every kind of malevolent being

morph.note: कर is √कृ + ट (-अ), an agent suffix that occurs only at the end of a compound (upapada): ‘-maker’.
Ablative of the action noun पठन ‘reading, recitation’: ‘from the reading alone’ — एव restricts the cause to the recitation itself.
Action noun in -अन from the causative stem नाशय- of √नश्, used as an agent: ‘destroyer’.

mantras.anvaya: (एतत् माहात्म्यम्) अशेषाणां दुर्वृत्तानां परं बलहानिकरम्, पठनात् एव रक्षोभूतपिशाचानां नाशनम् (भवति)।
mantras.anvaya_en: As in 12.18, two nominal predicates of the unexpressed subject माहात्म्यम्.
mantras.lit: (It is) supremely the destroyer of the strength of all the wicked; by its mere reading, the destroyer of rākṣasas, bhūtas and piśācas.
mantras.tr: It utterly breaks the power of all evil-doers, and by its recitation alone it destroys demons, ghosts and goblins.
mantras.tr_note: रक्षस्, भूत and पिशाच are classes of malevolent beings; ‘demons, ghosts and goblins’ is an approximation.

comm.t: The recitation is said to break the power of evil-doers and, by the mere act of reading (पठनादेव), to destroy three classes of malevolent beings: rākṣasas, bhūtas and piśācas.
A modern reading: the verse moves from human wrongdoers to unseen terrors. In both cases the protection named is the same — the remembered story of the Goddess’s victory.

Visarga before t becomes s; तथा + उत्तमैः → तथोत्तमैः (ā + u → o).

samasa.vigraha: पशवश्च पुष्पाणि च अर्घ्याणि च धूपाश्च, तैः
samasa.literal: with animals, flowers, arghya-waters and incense
samasa.sense: the offerings of a full worship
with sandal paste and lamps offered in worship

morph.note: कारक (√कृ + ण्वुल्) ‘maker’ as the last member of a compound; the second मम is its logical object: ‘causing my presence’.
A dvandva takes the gender of its last member (धूप, m.): masculine instrumental plural.

mantras.anvaya: मम एतत् सर्वं माहात्म्यं मम सन्निधिकारकम् (अस्ति)। पशुपुष्पार्घ्यधूपैः च तथा उत्तमैः गन्धदीपैः …
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line is a complete nominal sentence. The second line opens a new sentence, whose instrumentals continue through 12.21 to the main clause in 12.22 (प्रीतिः मे क्रियते …).
mantras.lit: This entire Māhātmya of mine brings about my presence. With animals, flowers, water-offerings and incense, and likewise with excellent perfumes and lamps —
mantras.tr: This whole account of my glory makes me present. With offerings of animals, flowers, water and incense, with the finest perfumes and lamps —
mantras.tr_note: The second line begins a sentence completed in 12.22 (‘the delight that is given me … by a year of worship is given me by a single hearing’).

comm.t: The first line restates 12.9: the whole Māhātmya makes the Devī present. The second line begins the list of a year’s worship — animal offerings (पशु), flowers, arghya, incense, perfumes, lamps — that will be weighed against one hearing of the text in 12.22.

The items named are the standard offerings of Purāṇic worship (upacāras). The mention of पशु reflects the animal offering of the Purāṇic rite; many Śākta communities offer a substitute instead, a practice the verse itself does not discuss.

sandhi.note: After a vowel other than a/ā, the visarga (रु) before a voiced sound appears as r; so also विविधैर्भोगैः, प्रदानैर्वत्सरेण.
Before a vowel the visarga after ai likewise appears as r.

sandhi.rule: described in words: the final n of अहन् is replaced by r (रु) in such compounds
sandhi.note: अहन् ‘day’ appears as अहर् before the second member; compare अहरहः ‘day after day’.

samasa.sense: continually; the neuter accusative is used as an adverb

morph.note: Gerundive in -अनीय of प्र + √उक्ष्, ‘what is to be sprinkled’, used as a noun for the consecrated water sprinkled in worship (and the rites of sprinkling).
Instrumental of time within which something is accomplished: ‘in (the course of) a year’.
Feminine relative pronoun anticipating प्रीतिः in 12.22; its correlative is सा there.

mantras.anvaya: (पशुपुष्पार्घ्यधूपैः …) विप्राणां भोजनैः होमैः अहर्निशं प्रोक्षणीयैः अन्यैः च विविधैः भोगैः प्रदानैः (च) वत्सरेण या (प्रीतिः मे क्रियते) …
mantras.anvaya_en: A continuation of the list of instrumentals begun in 12.20; the relative या opens the clause that 12.22 completes (या प्रीतिः मे क्रियते, सा …).
mantras.lit: with feedings of brāhmaṇas, with fire oblations, with sprinklings day and night, and with various other enjoyments and gifts — the (delight) which, in a year, …
mantras.tr: with the feeding of brāhmaṇas, with oblations and lustrations day and night, with every other kind of offering and gift — the delight these give me in a whole year
mantras.tr_note: ‘The delight … give me’ anticipates प्रीतिः मे क्रियते of 12.22, to which the relative या points; the sentence is completed there.

comm.t: The list of a year’s worship continues: feeding brāhmaṇas, homa, sprinkling with consecrated water day and night, other offerings and gifts. The relative या, ‘which’, prepares the comparison of 12.22: all this, over a year, pleases the Devī no more than a single hearing of her story.
A modern reading: the long catalogue of 12.20–21 is built up only to be outweighed. The rhetorical point is the value of attentive hearing, set against an entire year of costly ritual.

flags.uncertain: The analysis of या depends on 12.22 (प्रीतिर्मे क्रियते सास्मिन्), outside this batch: या is taken as the relative of प्रीतिः, with सा as correlative.
